description: S458 2a-fix F1: `bind:value` on a position that carries NO refinement writes the cell, even when the cell's type needs the whole-type judge. `@p.name` is an unrefined field of a struct with a refined field (`n: number(>0)`), and `@u` is a union `number(>0) | string`. Typing "bob" / "hello" writes both. In slice 2a the bind:value gate read a placeholder predicate off the whole-type stamp and emitted `if (false)`, so neither input ever wrote its cell.
rationale: §53.7.2: "bind:value on a constrained variable SHALL emit a runtime check at every input event, before the reactive assignment is applied. If the check fails, the assignment is not applied" — the check is the bound value's own constraint: `name` has none, and "hello" inhabits the `string` member of `number(>0) | string` (§53.3.1).
